purpose: Prevent repeated multi-hour debugging loops while preserving healthy forward progress and avoiding needless restart/recovery work.
milestone_definition: candidate install/recovery completed and identity verified
Phase 2 lane reaches a defined deliverable/acceptance gate

progress_timer: The 30-minute clock measures time since the last measurable forward progress, NOT elapsed time since the attempt began.
Every measurable progress event resets the 30-minute stall clock.
A healthy bounded operation may run longer than 30 minutes without interruption when its watchdog/expected-duration evidence remains good.
at_30_minutes_without_measurable_forward: At the next safe boundary, stop only the stalled mechanism, not the entire transaction.
Preserve the current install/session/snapshot/checkpoint whenever safety and identity remain proven.
Preserve evidence and classify the failure domain.
Pivot to a materially different mechanism or continue from the preserved checkpoint with a different mechanism.
Do NOT reinstall/reboot/recover/restart from zero solely because the 30-minute budget expired.
retry_rule: One retry maximum per failure class.
A retry is legal only when the mechanism materially changes and new evidence explains why it should succeed.
Parameter-only tweaking of the same failed mechanism is not a new mechanism.
at_60_minutes_without_lifecycle_progress: Do not terminate a healthy critical-path operation merely because 60 minutes elapsed.
Activate ready offline-safe independent Cart 2.0 lanes in parallel when they will not contend with or invalidate the live critical path.
The purpose of the 60-minute rule is to eliminate idle project time, not to restart healthy work.
restart_minimization: Prefer continuation from the current verified state over restart.
Recovery/reinstall/reboot is permitted only when required by device/runtime safety, identity uncertainty, transaction contract, or an actual Foundation gate failure.
A host/harness/transport failure alone must not cause device recovery if device identity/health and renderer state remain proven.
Required long-running gates must not be reset solely for orchestration-policy timing.
build_and_actions: Do not rebuild firmware or use GitHub Actions for host, transport, harness, telemetry-reader, or orchestration defects unless the existing artifact itself is invalidated.
Prefer exact existing artifacts and local/direct mechanisms.
attempt_contract: Before each live attempt record start time, expected bounded duration, material target, measurable progress signal, hard exit condition, failure class, and fallback mechanism.
Record last_forward_progress_at and the evidence that reset the stall clock.
A worker may not enter an open-ended debug loop.
required_long_running_gate_exception: A required long-running gate such as the >=90-minute Foundation soak is healthy progress while its required samples/uptime/state changes continue and watchdog conditions remain clean.
The soak runs uninterrupted unless its own acceptance/failure criteria fire.
Parallel offline-safe lanes should run during the soak when they cannot interfere with qualification.
reporting: Report elapsed wall-clock against material/lifecycle progress, not commit/test activity.
If a stall budget expires, record the pivot, preserved state, and why no restart was required or why a restart was objectively required.

current_seq39_application.rule: Apply immediately to active seq39. The ongoing 28-kernel sweep is healthy progress while profile count/telemetry advances. Do not stop, reinstall, recover, reboot, or restart it because a timer elapsed. Only if there is 30 minutes with no measurable forward progress should the stalled mechanism be stopped at a safe boundary and changed while preserving verified transaction state wherever possible.
current_seq39_application.soak_rule: Once the >=90-minute soak starts and remains healthy, keep it running uninterrupted; its continuing samples/state changes are measurable progress. Run offline-safe Phase 2 work in parallel when noncontending.

measurable_forward_progress: a bounded operation is actively running, healthy, and still within its expected duration
a required install, verification, sweep, soak, recovery, or acceptance phase advances
new decisive evidence closes or materially narrows the active failure
an independent lane reaches a defined deliverable or gate
not_progress: repeating the same failed mechanism without new evidence
parameter tweaking that does not change the failure mechanism
waiting on a hung/stale operation beyond its bounded expected duration
commits/tests/logging that do not advance or materially de-risk an active gate
